title: Estimating the Fisher information from ARPES in general two-band models
abstract: The Quantum Fisher information is frequently studied in the fields of quantum sensing and quantum metrology, as it specifies the sensitivity of a sensor through the Crámer-Rao bound, and in condensed matter physics where it relates to the quantum metric. Measuring the quantum Fisher information is therefore of significant current interest. In this work, we propose a scheme for measuring the quantum Fisher information with respect to any parameter in a general two-band solid state system using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy with carefully tuned incidence angles and light polarization. We investigate conditions under which this can be related back to information about the ground state of the material itself changing with system parameters.
summary: This paper presents a novel theoretical and experimental scheme to measure the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) in two-band solid state systems using Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES). By relating the QFI to the Classical Fisher Information derived from Pauli measurements, the authors provide a pathway to probe fundamental quantum properties, such as the quantum metric or strain response, using tunable light polarization and incidence angles.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of estimating the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) for a quantum state in a general two-band solid state system using Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES). It seeks to establish a measurable link between the theoretical QFI and experimentally accessible quantities.
main_result: The authors propose a detailed experimental scheme that relates the QFI to the Classical Fisher Information (CFI) derived from Pauli measurements, which can be measured by tuning ARPES incidence angles and light polarization.
method: The methodology involves deriving the CFI from the measured photoemission intensity, which is proportional to a Pauli measurement observable. This requires advanced reconstruction techniques using multiple polarization measurements (e.g., EDAC code) to determine the necessary polarization vectors.
model_or_system: The study focuses on general two-band solid state systems, exemplified by 2D materials like graphene and hexagonal boron phosphide (hBP). The physics is described using a Bloch Hamiltonian and analyzed via ARPES measurements of the photoemission intensity.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Classical Fisher Information (CFI), Quantum Metric, ARPES intensity $I(E, \mathbf{k}_f, \omega)$, and the dichroism coefficient (CDAC).
important_parameters: System parameters ($\lambda$) such as strain, incidence angles ($	heta_{	ext{inc}}, \phi_{	ext{inc}}$), and light polarization ($\alpha, \delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes rapid photoionization and approximates the final state as a scattered wave. Furthermore, the optimal measurement basis requires careful selection of polarization vectors to satisfy specific symmetry conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the conceptual flow from Hamiltonian to QFI to CFI to ARPES measurement. Later figures show the numerically calculated optimal polarization angles required to measure the QFI response to strain or other parameters for graphene and hBP.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical link between QFI and measurable CFI via Pauli measurements. It then details the experimental implementation using ARPES, involving the reconstruction of orbital matrix elements from multiple polarization measurements. Finally, it applies this framework to calculate the QFI response to external perturbations like strain for graphene and hBP.
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental quantum information theory (QFI) with cutting-edge experimental condensed matter spectroscopy (ARPES). The ability to map a theoretical quantum metric onto a measurable optical observable is highly relevant for quantum sensing applications in solid-state physics.
